explanation: The original reset synchronization logic incorrectly used asynchronous reset signals from the opposite clock domain directly in sensitivity lists, causing metastability and improper reset propagation. The fix implements proper two-flop synchronizers for each domain: output_rst is synchronized into input_clk domain (output_rst_sync1/2), and input_rst is synchronized into output_clk domain (input_rst_sync1/2). Combined reset signals (input_rst_combined = input_rst | output_rst_sync2, output_rst_combined = output_rst | input_rst_sync2) are then used as asynchronous resets for all sequential logic in their respective domains. This ensures that a reset on either side flushes all pre-reset state (pointers, gray-code pointers, valid flags) across both clock domains, preventing stale transfers after reset. Memory contents are not explicitly cleared (RAM), but pointers reset to zero so old data is never read after reset.
